recent_articles.title: Inclusion of Maithili in CBSE curriculum will connect future generation to their roots: Bihar CM - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Bihar Chief Minister Samrat Choudhary** hailed the decision by the **Central Board of Secondary Education (CBSE)** to include Maithili as a subject at the secondary level starting in 2026-27.  The move, supported by **BJP leader Gopal Ji Thakur**, was requested by Mr. Thakur and confirmed by **Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan** and **Minister of State for Education Jayant Chaudhary**. **Sanjay Saraogi**, Bihar BJP President, also welcomed the decision as a tribute to Maithili's cultural heritage and linguistic pride.  Mr. Saraogi emphasized that the inclusion will promote language learning and cultural understanding among future generations.

recent_articles.title: Bihar CM woos investors with amended package, says govt.’s top priority is ensuring safety - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Samrat Choudhary**, the Chief Minister of Bihar, emphasized the government's commitment to ensuring the security of businessmen and boosting industrial growth in the state. He inaugurated a business conclave organized by the **Bihar Chamber of Commerce and Industries** to mark its centenary year. The CM highlighted the "Bihar Industrial Investment Promotion Package-2025" aimed at attracting private investment, while assuring investors that their safety is paramount. Choudhary also addressed concerns about crime and caste politics, stating that criminals are not defined by their background and the government will prioritize investor security.

recent_articles.title: Govt. to soon bring in an AI policy to transform Bihar: CM - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Bihar Chief Minister Samrat Choudhary** announced the state government's intention to introduce an AI policy, aiming to transform Bihar into an AI hub.  He highlighted the potential of AI in India's communication revolution and emphasized the importance of collaboration with younger generations. The summit, organized by the IT Department in collaboration with the **Bihar Industries Association (BIA)** and Qlass EdTech, saw participation from Deputy Chief Minister **Bijendra Prasad Yadav**, Information Technology Minister **Nitish Mishra**, and founder of BharatGPT **Ankush Agrawal**.

recent_articles.title: One month of Samrat Choudhary Government in Bihar - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Samrat Choudhary**, the leader of the **Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP)**, took office as Chief Minister of Bihar on April 15, 2026.  He has implemented several initiatives focusing on development and combating corruption, including a blueprint for 11 satellite townships across 10 districts. The government also launched the "Police Didi Scheme" to enhance women's safety, established a three-tier public support system, and approved significant funding for education and infrastructure projects. Choudhary has also introduced measures to promote transparency in private schools and prioritize local contractors on civil projects.

recent_articles.title: Nazara Technologies shares soar 18% amid reports of Nikhil Kamath upping stake in block deal - The Economic Times
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Nazara Technologies** reported a significant increase in net profit for Q4FY26, driven by lower expenses and strong revenue growth in its gaming segment. The company's founder, **Nitish Mittersain**, is selling his stake in the company, while **Nikhil Kamath** of **Zerodha** and **Axana Estates** are among potential buyers.  The company also announced plans to acquire a controlling stake in a Spanish gaming studio for $100.3 million and invest in other companies within its core business segments of gaming, esports, and ad tech.

recent_articles.title: Nitish and BJP have no moral right to speak on dynastic politics, says Tejashwi Yadav - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Tejashwi Yadav**, leader of the opposition in Bihar's Legislative Assembly, criticized **Nitish Kumar** and **Prime Minister Narendra Modi** for their involvement in dynasty politics following the expansion of the **Bihar Cabinet**.  Yadav argued that both the **BJP** and its allies are engaging in dynasty politics, citing examples like the inclusion of sons of former Chief Ministers in the new cabinet.

recent_articles.title: Nitish Kumar’s son Nishant among 32 to take oath as Bihar Ministers - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Nitish Kumar's** son, **Nishant Kumar**, and 30 others were sworn in as ministers in the Bihar government on Thursday.  The ceremony was attended by Prime Minister **Narendra Modi**, Home Minister **Amit Shah**, and other senior leaders of the ruling NDA. **Samrat Choudhary**, who took over as Chief Minister after **Nitish Kumar** resigned, expanded his cabinet with former Deputy Chief Minister **Vijay Kumar Sinha**, and former Ministers **Shrawon Kumar** and **Ashok Choudhary**.  The oath-taking ceremony was presided over by Governor Lt. Gen. (Retd) Syed Ata Hasnain.

recent_articles.title: Nitish Kumar’s son Nishant Kumar may join Bihar cabinet on May 7 - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Nitish Kumar's** son, **Nishant Kumar**, is a subject of speculation regarding his potential inclusion in the new **Samrat Choudhary**-led NDA government cabinet.  Senior **JD(U)** leaders met with **Nitish Kumar** and held meetings in Patna ahead of the Cabinet expansion scheduled for Thursday. The event will be attended by Prime Minister **Narendra Modi**, Union Home Minister **Narendra Modi**, BJP president **Nitin Nabin**, and other senior NDA leaders, but no official confirmation has been made regarding **Nishant Kumar's** inclusion.  The administration is preparing for the ceremony at Gandhi Maidan with security personnel, police dogs, and waterproof tents to ensure a smooth event despite weather warnings of hailstorms and rain.

recent_articles.title: Bihar Cabinet expansion on May 7, Modi, Shah and Nabin to attend event - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Prime Minister Narendra Modi**, **Union Home Minister Amit Shah**, and **BJP president Nitin Nabin** will be present for the expansion of the **Bihar Cabinet** in Patna on Thursday, May 7, 2026.  The event is expected to feature most members from the previous Nitish Kumar-led NDA government retained, with a few new faces added to fill all 36 berths. The **BJP** aims for a "gala event" and preparations are underway at Gandhi Maidan. **Jitan Ram Manjhi**, leader of the HAM (S), has stated he will not demand a Cabinet berth and is content with whatever is offered.  The expansion is expected to include some new faces, potentially more women Ministers, and may see the return of several existing ministers from both the JD(U) and BJP.

recent_articles.title: Nishant launches Sadbhav Yatra from Bihar’s West Champaran - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Nishant Kumar**, son of former Bihar Chief Minister **Nitish Kumar**, launched his 'Sadbhav Yatra' from Bagaha, following in his father's footsteps.  The young leader was accompanied by **Umesh Singh Kushwaha**, the **Bihar JD(U) president**, and **Shrawon Kumar**, the **JD-(U) Legislature Party leader**. He addressed supporters along the route, emphasizing harmony and development for Bihar. The journey is seen as a significant step in Nishant Kumar's political career, potentially bolstering the **JD(U)** after the resignation of his father.

recent_articles.title: Nishant launches Sadbhav Yatra from Bihar’s West Champaran - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Nishant Kumar**, son of former Bihar Chief Minister **Nitish Kumar**, launched his "Sadbhav Yatra" from Bagaha in West Champaran district on Sunday, May 3, 2026.  The young leader was accompanied by **Umesh Singh Kushwaha**, the **Bihar JD(U)** president and **Shrawon Kumar**, the JD(U) Legislature Party leader. The yatra is seen as a significant step in Nishant Kumar's political career, following his father's long-held tradition of launching all yatras from Champaran.  He addressed supporters along the route, emphasizing the importance of harmony and development for Bihar.

recent_articles.title: Bihar CM Samrat Choudhary proposes system where the children of Ministers and the poor study together - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Samrat Choudhary**, Bihar Chief Minister, visited Nalanda for the first time since assuming office on Friday. He praised former Chief Minister **Nitish Kumar**'s development work in Nalanda and across the state while highlighting that Bihar is progressing under the leadership of **Prime Minister Narendra Modi** and **Nitish Kumar**.

recent_articles.title: Bihar govt removes Sanjay Gandhi's name from Patna zoo, dairy technology institute - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **The BJP-led government in Bihar** renamed the Sanjay Gandhi Biological Park as 'Patna Zoo' and the Sanjay Gandhi Institute of Dairy Technology as 'Bihar State Institute of Dairy Technology'. The cabinet also approved ₹23,165 crore for a power subsidy scheme, ₹104 crore for degree colleges under the 'Saat Nischay-3' program, and land for a Centre of Excellence for autism treatment.  The government allocated funds for four major road projects, increased monthly stipends for SC/ST students in hostels, and approved the development of model schools with modern labs.

recent_articles.title: BJP-led NDA govt. in Bihar likely to see Cabinet expansion on May 6 - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Samrat Choudhary**, the leader of the NDA government in Bihar, is planning a Cabinet expansion on May 6th.  The expansion is expected to include 16 Ministers each for the **Bharatiya Janata Party** and **Janata Dal (United)**, with smaller allies receiving four Ministers. The new Cabinet will likely feature many members from Nitish Kumar's previous administration.

recent_articles.title: BJP-led NDA govt. in Bihar likely to see Cabinet expansion on May 6 - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Samrat Choudhary**, the leader of the NDA government in Bihar, is preparing for a Cabinet expansion on May 6th.  Speculation suggests that **Bharatiya Janata Party** and **Janata Dal (United)** will each appoint 16 Ministers, while smaller allies will receive four. The expansion may include many familiar faces from Nitish Kumar's previous cabinet due to the Constitutional limit of a maximum of 36 ministers in the state.

recent_articles.title: Will take strict action against officials who hold up files for more than a month, says Bihar CM - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Samrat Choudhary**, the Chief Minister of **Bihar**, visited his ancestral village, Lakhanpur, on Sunday (April 26, 2026).  During a public meeting in Munger, he addressed concerns about red-tape and promised strict action against officials delaying file processing. He also emphasized his government's goal of providing basic amenities to all residents and ensuring accessible government services for everyone.

recent_articles.title: Samrat Choudhary approves funds for 75 ITI in first Cabinet meeting as Bihar CM - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Chief Minister Samrat Choudhary** approved several initiatives during his first Cabinet meeting, including the establishment of 75 state-of-the-art Industrial Training Institutes (ITIs) under the **PM SETU** scheme. The Cabinet also sanctioned ₹305 crore for an 11-acre research park at IIT Patna and an additional grant of ₹39 crore for phase 2 of the Incubation Centre at IIT Patna.  The State Cabinet also decided to develop 11 new satellite townships in the state, prohibiting land sales and construction until a Master Plan is prepared.

recent_articles.title: Kejriwal asks people of Tamil Nadu not to vote for NDA, says BJP has captured AIADMK - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Arvind Kejriwal**, leader of the **Aam Aadmi Party**, criticized the **AIADMK** for bringing the **BJP** to Tamil Nadu, claiming it would lead to the dismantling of the party and a loss of progress. He warned voters against supporting the BJP or the AIADMK, stating that their policies would halt the good work being done by the **DMK** government in Tamil Nadu.  Kejriwal praised **M.K. Stalin**, the Chief Minister of Tamil Nadu, for his initiatives like the "Chief Minister's Breakfast Scheme" and monthly stipends for women and girls.

recent_articles.title: JD(U) authorises Nitish Kumar to select new Bihar legislature party leader - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Nitish Kumar**, the former Chief Minister of Bihar, resigned from his position and was authorized by **the Janata Dal (United)** to select a new leader for their legislature party. The decision was made unanimously during a meeting held at 1, Anne Marg, with **Neeraj Kumar**, JD(U) chief spokesperson, confirming the authorization.

recent_articles.title: ​A plan of change: On Bihar politics and the BJP - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Samrat Choudhary**, a former member of the Rashtriya Janata Dal and Janata Dal (United), was sworn in as the 24th Chief Minister of Bihar on April 15, 2026.  This marks the first time a politician from the **Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP)** has held the office. The BJP's strategy for growth involved outgrowing regional partners and shifting power dynamics within the state, culminating in Choudhary's appointment after years of maneuvering.  The move signifies a shift in Bihar's political landscape as the BJP seeks to solidify its hold on the OBC-EBC base that was previously held by **Nitish Kumar**.

recent_articles.title: Edappadi Palaniswami interview: We know how to bring debt under control and implement all welfare schemes, says AIADMK leader - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Edappadi K. Palaniswami**, leader of the AIADMK, spoke to The Hindu about the upcoming Tamil Nadu Assembly elections and his party's alliance with the BJP. He addressed criticism from **M.K. Stalin**, Chief Minister of Tamil Nadu, regarding the delimitation bill and the 33% quota for women in Parliament and Legislative Assemblies. Palaniswami emphasized that the AIADMK will form a government and provide good governance. He also discussed his party's campaign strategy and its alliance with the BJP, stating they are united in their goal of ousting the DMK.  The article highlights Palaniswami's stance on youth empowerment and his party's efforts to attract young voters.

recent_articles.title: Bihar CM slams opposition over women's quota bill - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Bihar Chief Minister Samrat Choudhary** criticized the opposition parties for their refusal to support an amendment to the women's reservation bill, calling it a "black day" and vowing retaliation. **Sanjay Saraogi**, state party president of the BJP, announced that the party's women's wing would hold a protest on April 20th against the opposition's stance. The amendment, which grants 33% reservation to women in Parliament, was passed by an overwhelming majority in 2023 but faced opposition from non-NDA parties who were wary of its link with delimitation.

recent_articles.title: JD(U) likely to elect new head of legislature party at Patna meet on April 20 - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **JD(U)** is expected to elect a new legislature leader on April 20, 2026, following the resignation of **Nitish Kumar**, who was replaced by **Samrat Choudhary**. The meeting will be held in Patna at **Kumar's** new address. Speculation surrounds senior leader **Vijay Kumar Chaudhary**, currently one of two Deputy Chief Ministers, as a possible candidate for the position.  The party post has been vacant since **Kumar's** resignation on April 14th.

recent_articles.title: Bihar CM Samrat Choudhary launches self-enumeration phase of Census 2027 - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Bihar Chief Minister Samrat Choudhary** launched the self-enumeration phase of Census 2027 from the Chief Minister’s Secretariat, urging citizens to participate in the process. The initiative will be conducted digitally from April 17th to May 1st and includes a House Listing Operations (HLO) phase from May 2nd to May 31st. **Mr. Choudhary** emphasized the importance of accurate data for good governance and development plans, while **former Chief Minister Nitish Kumar** also completed his self-enumeration.  The web-based platform allows citizens to enter their family details online at their convenience.

recent_articles.title: Beneath the euphoria, Bihar’s first BJP Chief Minister faces several significant challenges - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: Newly sworn-in **Chief Minister Samrat Choudhary**, a former Deputy Chief Minister in the previous Nitish Kumar government, faces significant challenges as he assumes leadership of Bihar.  **Choudhary**, who joined the BJP in 2017 after a career in opposition parties, must navigate complex coalition dynamics and match the political persona of his predecessor while managing high expectations from the people. He also needs to address financial mismanagement, communal harmony concerns, and doubts about his abilities within the BJP and its ideological parent organization, the Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh (RSS).  **Choudhary** will need to establish his administrative capabilities in a state known for groupism among bureaucrats and broaden the BJP's voter base while maintaining alliances with existing parties.

recent_articles.title: Samrat Choudhary sworn in as Bihar’s first BJP CM - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Samrat Choudhary**, newly elected leader of the **National Democratic Alliance (NDA)**, was sworn in as the Chief Minister of Bihar on Wednesday.  He was accompanied by two senior JD(U) leaders, **Bijendra Prasad Yadav** and **Vijay Kumar Choudhary**, who are expected to serve as Deputy CMs. The swearing-in ceremony took place at Lok Bhawan with prominent figures from the BJP and former CM Nitish Kumar in attendance.  The new government is expected to expand after the results of upcoming state elections.

recent_articles.title: Bihar political history timeline: 1990 to 2026 - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Nitish Kumar**, the long-serving Chief Minister of Bihar, is set to resign on April 14, 2026, after a two-decade tenure.  Kumar's resignation follows his successful re-election as Chief Minister in 2025 and his nomination for the Rajya Sabha. The BJP will appoint its first Chief Minister in the state, marking a significant shift in Bihar's political landscape. Kumar's departure opens the door for a new chapter in Bihar's governance.

recent_articles.title: Nitish Kumar exits as Bihar Chief Minister, marks end of an era - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Nitish Kumar**, the former Chief Minister of Bihar, resigned on April 14, 2026, marking the end of his two-decade tenure.  The **Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP)** will now lead the government in Bihar for the first time.  Kumar's resignation follows a period marked by political shifts and criticism over his administration's focus on "obvious developments" while neglecting broader economic growth. He served as Chief Minister for ten terms, navigating complex socio-political terrain and promoting governance initiatives aimed at inclusivity and development. Kumar's legacy is one of both achievements and controversies, with critics questioning the effectiveness of his policies despite his efforts to improve law and order.  He will now take oath as a member of the Rajya Sabha on April 15th.

recent_articles.title: Bihar to get new CM as Nitish Kumar likely to resign today | LIVE updates - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Nitish Kumar**, the Chief Minister of Bihar, is expected to resign today, April 14, 2026, after his last Cabinet meeting. He will address party and NDA legislature meetings where the new leader's name will be announced. The **Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP)** is set to have its first Chief Minister in the state, with several BJP leaders being considered for the position. Prime Minister **Narendra Modi** is expected to attend the swearing-in ceremony on April 15th at Lok Bhawan.
